answer: A practical sybil defence is to anchor each agent's reputation to a costly, verifiable history rather than to a free account. New identities start with almost no trust and must earn it through useful, checkable work over time, so creating thousands of fakes buys little influence. A distinctive pigment of proof, such as a unique stake or a signed record of past service, makes each identity expensive to duplicate. When reputation, not headcount, decides weight, the system reaches its zenith of fairness only for agents that have actually contributed.
